clue.text: Bookish lady's book — draw short sword on family in it

indicators.note: it refers back to the draw word, so the sword and family go inside that word

parts.note: to lug is to drag or draw something heavy

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on the next, so the sword comes before the family

parts.note: an estoc is a thrusting sword of the late Middle Ages
kin are one's family or relations

explanation.surface: A scholarly woman's book describes drawing a sword against her own family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the draw, so 'in it' means the sword and family sit inside that word; an estoc is an obscure name for a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluestocking is a scholarly, intellectual woman, named after an 18th-century literary circle.

clue.text: Unemployed and unrated and with no opening — terrible

indicators.note: terrible suggests things gone badly wrong, so these letters are jumbled
the word and loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A jobless person, without a rating and with no way in, feels awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no opening' cuts AND to ND; 'terrible' shuffles UNRATED + ND into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers made redundant have lost their jobs because the work is no longer needed, so they are unemployed.

clue.text: Greenhorn left in mountainous region

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner or novice

explanation.surface: An inexperienced climber is abandoned in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region straddling Austria and Italy.

clue.text: The poet with the gravy

definitions.meaning: a colouring sauce used to darken gravy, a British kitchen staple

explanation.surface: A poet turns up alongside the gravy at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the poet Robert Browning is also the name of a gravy colouring.

clue.text: Where accidents are affecting the roses

definitions.meaning: a stretch of road where crashes happen often
a fungal disease that marks rose leaves with dark patches

explanation.surface: Something is going wrong with the roses wherever accidents happen.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident black spot is a dangerous stretch of road; black spot is also a common fungal disease of roses.

clue.text: Piece soup?

indicators.note: the question mark hints that the word soup is not what it seems and should be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bowl of soup is offered as a work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, a piece.

clue.text: Crazy on a nude, awfully sweet

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is mad about a nude painting, which they find terribly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut sundae is an ice-cream dessert, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Girl I complain about

indicators.note: about turns the whole run I followed by the complaint word round

parts.note: to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to grumbling about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses I + MOAN as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a girl's name, Ruth's mother-in-law in the Bible.

clue.text: Run a novel audit producing assessment that's too low

indicators.note: producing signals that the words before it are worked into something new

explanation.surface: An unusual audit produces a valuation that is too low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'producing' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Undervaluation is assessing something at less than its true worth.

clue.text: Scrambled eggs endorsed for firefighter

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firefighter gives approval to scrambled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Green Goddesses were old British Army fire engines brought out when firefighters went on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Goddess was a British army fire engine used for emergency firefighting.

clue.text: Melodious piece of English used in Peterborough, formerly

indicators.note: the piece of English goes inside the old district name

parts.note: the Soke of Peterborough was a historic administrative area of England, abolished in 1965

indicators.note: only a run of letters from inside the word English is taken

explanation.surface: A tuneful snatch of English was once heard in Peterborough, an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterborough has been a city in Cambridgeshire since 1974; 'formerly' points to its old Soke, a separate historic district until 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: Songlike means resembling a song, so melodious.

clue.text: Glorious day for gilded youth

parts.note: the Glorious First of June, a 1794 British naval victory, written as June I and shortened to JUN I
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golden day is marked for privileged young people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious First of June was a British naval victory over France in 1794; JUN I is a short form of that date.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior is a young person, a youth.

clue.text: Organ adapted by reversing tube — till it squeaks?

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged
reversing means the tube word is written backwards

parts.note: a pipe is a tube

explanation.surface: An organ is modified by reversing one of its pipes until it squeaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' makes ORANG from ORGAN; 'by reversing' turns PIPE into EPIP. The definition plays on squeezing someone until the pips squeak.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is to squeeze someone until the pips squeak, as with an orange; the pip is what squeaks.

clue.text: Old man finds water bird slightly involved with detectives

indicators.note: only one letter of the detectives word gets tangled into the bird

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird
the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police detective headquarters

explanation.surface: An old man spots a water bird that has become a little mixed up with the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly involved with' moves just the Y of YARD into GREBE, giving GRE(Y)BE + ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A greybeard is an old man, from the colour of his beard.

clue.text: No long journey on little drink comes up for detective

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a trek is a long, arduous journey
a nip is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Instead of a long trip, a detective has a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' reverses the whole run NO + TREK + NIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Allan Pinkerton founded the famous American detective agency, so his name stands for a private detective.

clue.text: Divine seen in windows etc

indicators.note: seen in shows the answer sits inside the clue words

explanation.surface: Something holy is glimpsed in church windows and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to search for water underground with a rod, which is what dowsing means.

clue.text: A little bit was — what did you say about it? — total defeat?

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount, as in not a whit

indicators.note: the eh goes round it, meaning the word was

parts.note: eh is what you say when you didn't catch something

explanation.surface: A speaker asks someone to repeat something, puzzled about a crushing loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about it' tells you to wrap the puzzled interjection round the 'it', which here stands for the word was given just before.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a whitewash is a total defeat in which the loser fails to score or win a game.

clue.text: Equipment for partners in the Copper Belt

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment
West and East are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Gear for a pair of partners in Zambia's mining country.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named by compass points, and West partners East.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitwe is a mining city in Zambia's Copperbelt province, so it is a place in the Copper Belt.

clue.text: Fiddling about with money — two sovereigns involved

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money

indicators.note: involved means one ruler is wrapped up inside the other

parts.note: a king is one sovereign
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the other sovereign

explanation.surface: Someone is fiddling with cash involving a couple of gold coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also a British gold coin, which the surface plays on; ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the familiar royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinkering means making small, aimless adjustments, fiddling about.

clue.text: Parliament success: what about Mr Coe? Negative

indicators.note: the negative goes round the athlete's first name

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
Seb Coe is the British Olympic runner and politician

explanation.surface: A political win prompts a question about Lord Coe, answered with a no.
explanation.walkthrough: Naseby, 1645, was a decisive Parliamentarian victory in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Naseby was the Parliamentary army's great victory over Charles I.

clue.text: Cats or dogs have been muted

indicators.note: the words cats or dogs have the answer inside them

explanation.surface: The household pets have been quietened down.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordo is the Italian musical direction meaning muted or muffled.

clue.text: County changed date with support of the rest

parts.note: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: changed means the letters of date are rearranged

explanation.surface: A county altered the date with the backing of everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the frame of a bed, which supports you while you rest.

clue.text: Capital setter in resting place

indicators.note: in puts the setter inside the resting place

parts.note: a sofa is a place to rest
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is lying on a couch in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Produce another version of the colour of 2, with love

parts.note: 2-down's answer begins with a colour, the colour of danger
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone recreates the shade of an earlier item with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to do it again, producing a fresh version.

clue.text: A match with new foe in '80s film — no problem at all with this

indicators.note: in puts the match and foe inside the film

parts.note: Grease is the musical film; its sequel Grease 2 came out in 1982
a test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: new means the letters of foe are freshly rearranged

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture against an unfamiliar opponent appears in a musical film.
explanation.walkthrough: The original Grease is from 1978, so the clue's 80s film is loose; Grease 2 came out in 1982. 'new' rearranges the enemy before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with the greatest of ease means it gives no difficulty whatever.

clue.text: Leave codlin out for sovereign?

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: out means the codlin letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave a cooking apple out of the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: A codlin is a kind of cooking apple; 'out' shuffles it to LDCOIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a British gold coin, an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Trophy we lost like men

parts.note: as means like, as in as good as new
hes are males, the plural of he

explanation.surface: A team laments a lost prize, men being men.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series trophy between England and Australia; the British setter's we is England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the trophy contested in Test cricket between England and Australia.
